plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: A small deciduous tree that produces fragrant, five-petaled blossoms on bare branches before leaves emerge. It is widely cultivated in East Asian gardens and valued for both its ornamental flowers and its fruit, used in pickles and liqueurs.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (February to March)
plants.location: China, Japan, Korea; cultivated in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms are celebrated in Japan as heralds of spring, and they bloom earlier than cherry blossoms, sometimes opening amid lingering snow.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: A bulbous perennial with trumpet-shaped yellow flowers surrounded by paler yellow petals and slender gray-green leaves. It naturalizes in meadows, woodlands, and gardens, and numerous cultivars have been bred from it.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (March to April)
plants.location: Western Europe, especially the UK, France, and Spain; naturalized in North America
plants.funFact: Daffodils contain toxic alkaloids such as galantamine, which has been developed into a medication for Alzheimer's symptoms.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: An evergreen Australian tree or large shrub that covers itself in fluffy, fragrant golden flower balls. It grows in woodlands and dry forests and is a common sight in southern Australia as winter ends.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring in the Southern Hemisphere (July to October), with some blooming into early autumn in cooler regions
plants.funFact: Golden wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1.

plants.name: Crocus vernus
plants.description: A low-growing cormous perennial with goblet-shaped flowers that emerge in grassy areas, often through melting snow. Crocuses provide an important early nectar and pollen source for bees emerging from winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (February to April)
plants.location: Alps and Pyrenees mountains of Europe; widely cultivated in temperate gardens
plants.funFact: Although it is a spring bloomer, Crocus vernus is related to Crocus sativus, the source of saffron, which flowers in autumn.
